title: Clinical Mastery: Resolving CRVO vs. Diabetic Retinopathy
summary: A high-yield comparative analysis between a resolving Central Retinal Vein Occlusion (CRVO) and Diabetic Retinopathy (DR). Distinguishing these entities is critical for management, as CRVO requires ruling out underlying systemic vascular risk, while DR mandates glycemic control and metabolic optimization.

branches: CRVO: Thrombus in central vein, high-pressure outflow block
DR: Chronic endothelial cell dysfunction, microaneurysms, basement membrane thickening
Resolving CRVO: Venous tortuosity improves, collaterals form, disc edema regresses
Proliferative DR: Neovascularization secondary to chronic ischemia

sections.title: Red Flags: When to Worry
content: RAPD in CRVO (indicates >10 disc area of ischemia)

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Protocol
content: Step 1: Dilated Fundus Exam with 90D lens
Step 4: Systemic workup (BP, CBC, HbA1c, ESR/CRP for CRVO)

content.explanation: C: Check Pressure (IOP), R: Rule out systemic disease (BP/DM), V: VEGF inhibitors, O: Observe for collaterals.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Resolving CRVO often exhibits optociliary shunts; these are distinct from neovascularization.
DR never presents as a sudden '4-quadrant' explosive change unless vitreal hemorrhage occurs.
Always perform gonioscopy in ischemic CRVO before Anti-VEGF injection.
HbA1c optimization is the most potent long-term treatment for DR.
